REAL BUG: sae_parse_commit() calls sae_parse_token_container(sae,pos,end,token,token_len) unconditionally whenever h2e is set (:2253-2254), but pasn_responder.c:163, pasn_initiator.c:180, and wpa_supplicant/sme.c:1904 all call sae_parse_commit() with h2e hardcoded/derived true and token=token_len=NULL. sae_parse_token_container() (unlike its sibling sae_parse_commit_token, which does guard with if(token)/if(token_len)) writes *token=pos+3 and *token_len=pos[1]-1 with NO NULL check, so a remote peer sending an SAE Commit frame containing an Anti-Clogging Token Container element to PASN triggers a NULL pointer dereference/crash.

fns.desc: Already surfaced by sqc itself as findings at lines 1908/1909 (graded TP above): sae_parse_commit() calls sae_parse_token_container(sae,pos,end,token,token_len) unconditionally when h2e is set, but pasn_responder.c/pasn_initiator.c/sme.c call sae_parse_commit() with h2e forced true and token=token_len=NULL; sae_parse_token_container has no NULL guard (unlike its sibling sae_parse_commit_token) and writes through both -- remote NULL-deref DoS via a crafted SAE commit frame with a Token Container element.
